Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.
I’ll first read the workspace contract, the fish-control transfer protocol, and the required visual-evidence workflow. Then I’ll inspect the inherited rollout artifacts before touching the policy.

The visual-evidence skill applies because the sampled rollouts include keyframe sheets. I’ll use it to compare both views of the best finite rollout against the most informative failure, cross-checking metrics and diagnostics; only after that will I consult the bookshelf references and formulate the candidate hypothesis.

Both sampled sheets confirm self-propulsion in still water: a coherent alternating reverse-von-Kármán-style mid-plane street and paired 3D structures follow a target-directed arc. No sampled rollout is a semantic failure; the useful comparison is therefore the best v30 capture at 18.997 T against the repeated v29 captures at 19.311 T, with inherited left-domain near-miss evidence supplying the failure boundary. I’m now quantifying what v30 improved and where it still spends control authority before choosing one mechanism.

The assigned parent’s whole-wave pose projection is a genuine closed-loop improvement: capture advances by 0.314 T and the distance integral falls by 0.0250 L, with a 0.15–0.17 L lead from 8–16 T and unchanged peak speed/load. Its cost is a small rise in acceleration-limit residence (42.35%→43.43%). Following the required bookshelf protocol, I’m consulting the mechanism references now; any transfer will be limited to a body-frame, two-joint invariant and recorded with a falsification test.

The bookshelf transfer I’m adopting is phase-centered half-cycle asymmetry: infer the propulsive half-cycle from the oscillatory tail tangent, not from oscillation plus deliberate route/redirect curvature. This extends the now-validated mean-preserving pose separation into the actuator phase detector. On the completed v30 trace it changes steering by more than 0.05 on 24.6% of states (mean absolute 0.052, maximum 0.654), concentrated after 16 T, without touching raw redirect geometry or any scalar gait gain. I’m recording that diagnosis and falsification boundary before editing, as required by the visual workflow.

The policy now contains exactly one new architectural change: the half-cycle bend-side detector is centered by the already-computed route-plus-redirect mean tangent. I’m also promoting the parent’s newly completed v30 result from “offline diagnostic” to a durable closed-loop lesson; the new candidate’s own outcome remains explicitly unevaluated.

The candidate and durable guidance are both updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s prescribed check-runner now; it will run only the semantic-guidance, policy-contract, schema, and boundary checks—no CFD.

The configured check-runner could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this environment. The invocation itself was attempted; I’ll execute the exact three prescribed commands directly, separately, and repair any failure before finishing.

All three prescribed checks pass: the guidance change is semantic, the policy returns two finite commands with the frozen `L=64` adapter, and the solver boundary is clean. I’m doing one final deterministic audit of the exact delta, reflection behavior, parameter schema, and frozen-trace effect; this remains a no-CFD check.

Implemented exactly one v31 target-policy candidate.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:407) centers half-cycle detection by removing commanded route/redirect curvature.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:108) promotes whole-wave pose rejection to an evidence-backed reusable lesson.

All prescribed checks pass, including semantic-guidance, policy contract, 57-field schema, actuator-envelope, and solver-boundary validation. The configured check-runner model was unavailable, so its exact commands were run directly. No CFD was run.
